findings.summary: The supplied artifact supports with high confidence that the displayed 23×23 matrix has entries in {-1,+1} and absolute determinant 2,779,447,296,000,000. The verifier checks the matrix dimensions and entries, uses exact integer Bareiss elimination with pivoting, row-swap sign correction, and exact-division checks, and compares the computed determinant with the stated factor product.

No execution transcript or intermediate Bareiss pivots are included, so the large determinant arithmetic is not displayed step by step in the transaction. This is not considered a material defect because the complete matrix and deterministic exact verifier are supplied and independently replayable.

The verified matrix is an admissible 23×23 sign matrix, so its absolute determinant establishes D23 ≥ 2,779,447,296,000,000. This certifies the already published lower endpoint rather than improving it.

The transaction does not determine whether 2,779,447,296,000,000 is the exact value of D23. It verifies only one matrix and supplies no exhaustive enumeration, Gram-matrix classification, search certificate, impossibility proof for larger determinants, or other optimality argument.
The transaction supplies no witness exceeding 2,779,447,296,000,000. Its determinant equals the published lower endpoint, so it does not establish a strictly improved lower bound.

The transaction gives no argument concerning the stated real-valued upper estimate, its floor, determinant divisibility restrictions, or any other improved upper bound, and therefore does not establish a strictly lower upper endpoint.
